headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend intact, but the long-term trend is still repairing

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The uptrend is intact, so the current posture supports increasing acquisition budget, with emphasis on active-trader channels that tend to respond most in this phase. Confidence is medium rather than high because the longer-term trend is still recovering and price is well below its previous peak, so a staged increase fits better than a single large one. This is budget-posture guidance based on trailing data, not trading advice.

reasons: Price is 18% above its 200-day average; 90-day gain is about 40%.
Weekly RSI near 60 shows firm momentum without overbought conditions.
The 200-day average is still falling (-5.3% over 90 days), limiting conviction.
Price is 33% below its all-time high; Fear & Greed is 73 (Greed).
watch: The key tension is between fast recent gains and a slow-moving long-term trend: price is up about 40% in 90 days and above its 200-day average, yet that average is still declining and only 47% of recent days closed above it. If the 200-day slope turns flat or positive and breadth broadens, the uptrend read would be better supported; if price slips back under the 200-day average, the read would weaken. These are trailing measures, not forecasts.
analysis: Short-term mood is warm rather than euphoric. Fear & Greed sits at 73 (Greed) and funding is modestly positive (z-score +0.44), while longs outnumber shorts 1.42 to 1 and open interest is about $2.4B, so leverage does not look stretched. Options-implied volatility (DVOL 35.8) and the VIX (16.1) are both subdued, and realised volatility is mid-range at the 50th percentile.

Momentum is the strongest leg of the read: BTC is up roughly 40% over 90 days, weekly RSI is 59.8 (firm, not overbought), and the 50-day average sits about 8% above the 200-day. Participation is thinner than the headline gain implies, with only 47% of recent days closing above the 200-day average. ETFs took in about $31M on the latest day, and the next FOMC meeting on 2026-10-27 is the nearest scheduled macro event.

Over the long view, price is 18% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.18) and 1.27x its 200-week average, yet the 200-day line is still sloping down (-5.3% over 90 days) and price is 33% below its all-time high. That reads as a recovery rather than a mature bull. Macro is mixed, with the 10-year yield at 5.24% against a 3.63% fed funds rate, while cumulative ETF inflows of about $57.6B and roughly 1.28M BTC held by public companies point to sustained institutional holding.
